Welcome to Finance
Everything that costs or earns your business money, in one place. Track bills, loans and rentals, keep a register of properties, modifications and investments, plan with budgets, and see what you sold in Sales Reports.
POS Sales — Last 6 Months
Where the Money Goes
Approx. per month
Needs Attention
Finance Sections
Loading summary…
User Guide
Getting started

Set Finance up once and it keeps track of what is due for you. A good order is:

  1. Properties — add the shops, offices, land and warehouses you own or lease. Bills, rentals and modifications can then be linked to them.
  2. Bills — add regular costs such as electricity, water, internet, insurance and subscriptions.
  3. Loans and Rentals — add what you borrow and what you rent, with their repayment cadence.
  4. Investments and Budget — record capital you put in, and plan what you expect to spend.
  5. Come back to this Overview daily: the Needs attention list shows anything overdue or expiring.

Amounts per day or per year are converted to an approximate monthly figure (day × 30, year ÷ 12) so everything can be compared.

Bills

Create a bill

  1. Click Create Bill, enter a name and choose a category (choose Other to type your own).
  2. Choose Recurring (per day, month or year, plus the year the agreement is valid until) or One-time with a due date.
  3. Enter the amount, or tick amount varies by usage for meter-based bills — you enter the actual charge when paying.
  4. Optional: first instalment due date, a debit account, allow split payment, and a reminder a set number of days before it is due.
  5. Optional: assign it to a branch, department, property, employee, modification or rental so it appears on that record.

Pay a bill

  1. Open the bill and click Pay on the period you are paying.
  2. Choose Full, Partial (enter the amount) or Split (pay from two or more accounts).
  3. Every payment is listed on the bill's Transaction details tab. Past periods left unpaid show as Overdue.
Loans
  1. Click Add Loan and enter the facility name, lender bank and borrowed amount.
  2. Set the interest type and rate, the recurring cadence and the estimated number of periods.
  3. Enter the first instalment due date and, if known, the loan ending date.
  4. Pick the account repayments are deducted from and how many days before to remind you.
  5. The loan's Installment schedule tab lists every repayment and whether it is paid.

A loan counts as active until its ending date. The Loans tab totals the principal and approximate monthly outflow of active loans.

Rentals
  1. Click Add Rental, choose the property type and purpose, and enter any key money paid.
  2. Add the owner's contact and bank details so you know where to pay.
  3. Enter the recurring cost, how often it recurs, the first instalment due date and the year the agreement is valid until.
  4. The Billing schedule tab shows each period; pay from there. Linked bills lists bills assigned to this rental.
Properties
  1. Click Add Property and enter the property name, asset type (building, land, shop, vehicle, machinery…) and asset cost.
  2. If it has an agreement or licence that ends, tick This asset has an expiry date and enter the expiry date.
  3. Properties expiring within 60 days appear under Needs attention on this page.
Modifications
  1. Use Modifications for renovations, repairs and fit-outs. Click Add Modification.
  2. Enter a name, what it is assigned to, the estimated cost, the renovation or work type, a reference and the duration.
  3. Assign bills to the modification to see its real cost on the Linked bills tab.
Investments
  1. Click Add Investment and enter the plan name, type, provider and policy or reference number.
  2. Set the payment pattern, contribution amount, billing cadence, first payment date and the year to schedule through.
  3. Optional: maturity date, expected return, target amount and a reminder.
  4. Record each payment; the Contribution details tab shows progress towards the target.
Budget
  1. Click Add Budget and enter a name, a type (monthly or yearly) and a start date. The end date is set for you.
  2. Every budget starts with the standard categories; enter the planned amount for each.
  3. Click Log actual spend to record what you spent by category, month and amount, with a note, and compare planned against actual.
  4. Click Activate Budget to make it the one you are currently working to.
Sales Reports
  1. Pick a period — today, last 7 or 30 days, this month, quarter or year — or a custom From / To range.
  2. Narrow by branch / warehouse and by counter (a counter limits the report to POS sales).
  3. Use the tabs: Overview, Breakdown, Products & categories, Customers, Returns, By period and Transactions.
  4. Click Export for a PDF report or a CSV to open in Excel.
Financial Flow Chart
  1. Bills, loans and rentals sit on the left and flow into Expenses, which shows the approximate monthly total.
  2. Income sources — POS sales, quotations, invoices and credit recovery — sit on the right.
  3. Overdue items are outlined in red. Click any box to open that record or report.

Design tips & inspiration

Keep your palette to 3 colors — it reads cleaner and prints truer.

White space isn't empty — it's what makes the important things stand out.

Pick one bold font for headings, one quiet one for body text.

Flip it upside down — mistakes hide in familiar shapes, not unfamiliar ones.

Welcome to CRM
Group your leads into relations, track them through a pipeline, capture new ones with forms, and keep every contact and follow-up task in one place.
How CRM Works
A lead travels through five steps, from setup to a won sale. Each step below shows what happens, who usually does it and the ribbon button to use — click a button to jump straight there.
1
Set up
Admin · once
Add departments in CRM → Departments (they are shared with HR when you have it), and put people in them from Settings → Users. In Org Structure, link each department to a pipeline, pick the one marketing intake department, and set discount limits and follow-up days. Add the Stages leads move through, then give staff Permissions.
2
Capture leads
Marketing
Leads come in from published forms, a CSV/Excel import or by hand. Duplicates are matched by phone and email, and every new lead lands in the intake department first.
3
Route
Marketing
Marketing checks each new lead in the Marketing Inbox and forwards it to the department that should handle it. It then appears in that department's pipeline.
4
Work the deal
Sales team
Move the lead stage by stage on the Pipeline, call back on the follow-up days, and send a quotation. A discount above the department's limit goes to the head in Quotation Approvals.
5
Win & track
Managers
Mark a lead Won to create an invoice, sales order or project in one step. The customer stays in Contacts, and results show on the CRM Dashboard.
Words you'll see
Relation / PipelineA board of leads for one team or product. Called Pipeline Projects on the ribbon.
LeadOne enquiry from a person or company, moving through a pipeline.
StageA column on the pipeline board, e.g. New → Contacted → Quoted → Won.
Intake departmentThe single department (usually Marketing) where every new lead arrives first.
Follow-upA reminder to call a lead again, scheduled from the department's follow-up days.
ContactThe person or customer behind a lead, kept with all their activity.
Quick Tips
Track deals with Relations
Group leads into a relation and move them through your pipeline stage by stage.
Capture leads with Forms
Publish a form for a relation and new leads drop straight into its pipeline.
Keep contacts organized
Every customer and lead you talk to shows up in Contact with their activity.
Never miss a follow-up
Create tasks and track what's open, overdue or completed in Task.

    Billing Setup

    Add your recurring financial items. All optional — skip any and add later.

    Loans Track loans your business has taken — record the principal, interest rate and repayment schedule. Each payment reduces the outstanding balance so you can monitor debt and plan cash flow.
    Rentals Manage properties you rent out — set lease terms, monthly rent and log each collection. Overdue payments are flagged so you never miss a follow-up.
    Properties Register every building your business owns — shops, offices, warehouses and land. Record purchase value and address for asset tracking, linked to rentals and expenses.
    Bills Log recurring costs — utilities, subscriptions, rent and fixed overheads. Set amounts and due dates so nothing slips, and mark bills paid to keep accounts reconciled.
